patch_description:
The previous program failed validation for multiple structural reasons: it returned an empty `column_orderings` list (violating the required per-row orderings contract), mutated the dataframe shape by adding/dropping an "original_index" column, returned a dataframe whose columns were altered by internal bookkeeping, and its recursion contained broken invariants (e.g., `column_recursion` used positional `i` from `as_completed`, losing row identity; `final_result_df.columns` was assigned mismatched names). None of it aligned with the actual character-Trie prefix-cache objective.

The fix replaces the entire editable block with a clean, correct implementation that: (1) preserves every cell, row and column exactly; (2) builds 2–3 cheap candidate per-row column orderings (global frequency-ranked order with score sum(len(v)*count*(count-1)), a conditional partition tree using integer factorization and bincount that picks column orders per group, and a length-ranked fallback); (3) scores each candidate with the true objective — sum of LCPs of lexicographically adjacent serialized strings — using C-speed slice equality binary search; (4) returns the best candidate with `column_orderings[i][j]` naming the original column whose value sits at position j of row i, with the dataframe keeping original column names positionally. `col_merge` groups are kept adjacent as blocks in every ordering. Mixed types/NaN are handled by serializing only for scoring while outputting original values.
